name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Garcia holds an overwhelming financial edge, raising $1.17 million plus $562,000 in outside support while Fierro raised $485
District fundamentals favor Democrats by roughly 17 points on partisanship and about 30 on broader fundamentals
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%

model.rationale: Every available indicator points the same way: a D+17 Houston-area seat, a well-funded incumbent seeking re-election, a challenger with negligible resources, and markets pricing a near-certain Democratic win. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the structural baseline.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing a single-digit race, or an unusually strong Republican national environment, would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a Houston-area district that leans about 17 points Democratic. Her Republican challenger, Martha Fierro, has raised only a few hundred dollars, while Garcia has brought in roughly $1.2 million and benefits from more than $560,000 in outside support spent on her behalf. No outside groups are opposing her.

There are no public general-election polls and no major expert raters have weighed in, but prediction markets put the odds of a Democratic win near 98 percent. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with only modest uncertainty from the absence of polling.
